note: Universal layer: always rendered, whatever the format and genre. No genre-specific numbers here. Lower priority renders first; the renderer interleaves these rules with the format and genre lines and the hard cap drops the highest numbers first.

rules.text: UNIT: plan beats as action -> reaction (~70% plain pairs); at the beats that matter vary it: reaction first (the shock, then its cause), sound-only action (picture on the listener), reaction chain (one blow, several faces), withheld reaction (once or twice).
CAMERA: ONE move per shot, picked by the focal emotion and named with speed and end framing ("slow push-in to a close-up"); static by default; never stack moves.
CONTINUITY: keep the 180-degree side and screen direction; answer a look with what is seen; cut on action or on a look; keep light direction, wardrobe, props and positions within a scene.
SCALE: change size one step at a time, closer as tension rises; a wide-to-close-up jump only for a shock; never three cuts with the same size AND move.

AI VIDEO: one clear, simple action per shot that finishes within its length; no fast choreography, crowds in contact, readable text or fine finger work; body-part inserts (feet stopping, a hand on a strap, a back walking away) render reliably.
ACTING: eyes have a task (checking, avoiding, measuring); reactions start mid-line; the tighter the shot, the less movement.
ANGLE: eye level by default; low = dominance, high = smallness, Dutch tilt = instability (rare).
